title: Depression and social anxiety
summary: Woman in her 20s with severe recurrent depression and social anxiety, under the CMHT, living with her parents. Tests prompting (food, washing, medication), social support for engaging with others, a budgeting answer on the form that the notes contradict, and journeys she cannot make without her mother. She is physically well, so several activities are genuinely no difficulty.
exercises: medication prompting (3b) and failure likely to cause deterioration
social support from an experienced family member (9c)
status conflict: form vs notes on budgeting
planning and following journeys: psychological distress, 11e vs 11f
genuine nodiff activities in a mental health claim
repeatedly: washing only twice a week with prompting

conditions_in_documents: Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe

must_find.quote: Mum makes the dinner and tells me to come and help but most of the time I don't.
When her mother prompts and stays in the kitchen with her she will help with simple tasks.
she'll peel/chop if mum is there and keeps her at it. Without mum asking she won't come down.
Can use hob/oven, no physical problem. Mum "every day really".

gaps: No account of her preparing and cooking a whole simple meal even with prompting; only helping with tasks
Mother's presence is for motivation, not safety, so supervision (1e) is not supported
activities.draft_note: Needs prompting to prepare or cook on most days; nothing points to a safety risk: 1d, 2 points.
Poor appetite but eats what is put in front of her without reminders; missed meals come from not preparing food (activity 1).

must_find.quote: Mum reminds me about my tablets because I forget or I just don't bother.
she was missing doses most days, and her mood deteriorated. Adherence has been good since the reminders started.
Mum puts tablet next to her cup of tea every morning and checks.

gaps: No home therapy yet (on psychology waiting list), so 3c-3f are not in play
activities.draft_note: Daily prompting to take sertraline; missing doses led to deterioration: 3b, 1 point.

must_find.quote: I don't shower as much as I should. Mum has to go on at me.
she will not shower unless prompted, and that without prompting she has gone over a week without washing
Mum says "most days I'm on at her and most days it doesn't happen".

gaps: Even with prompting she showers only about twice a week; whether that is to an acceptable standard and as often as reasonably required is a point the reviewer could press
No statement from her mother yet
activities.draft_note: Will not wash without prompting: 4c, 2 points.
No difficulty reported in any document.

must_find.quote: I stay in my joggers most days. I can get dressed.
I have seen her on visits in the same clothes as the previous visit on several occasions.
Mum says if there's an appointment she has to tell her to get changed. Didn't say how often otherwise.

gaps: How often she needs prompting to dress or change is not recorded
Not clear whether she would get dressed and undressed each day at all without prompting
activities.draft_note: 6c(i) prompting is likely but the documents do not show it on over 50% of days; it would take daily living from 11 to 13.
Speaks and understands normally; avoiding strangers belongs under activity 9.
Can read and understand; her mother opening letters is avoidance, not a reading difficulty (relevant to activity 10).

must_find.quote: If I have to talk to someone I don't know my heart goes and I feel sick and I want to get out.
She does not engage with unfamiliar professionals without her mother, who has supported her through all of her appointments and knows how to calm her.
Mum has supported her through all of this since 2024 and knows what helps (breathing, letting her sit by the door).

gaps: Whether her mother counts as 'experienced' for social support needs stating explicitly
9d is arguable (left CMHT waiting room), but she does engage when her mother is there, so 9d is not supported over 50% of days
activities.draft_note: Engages only with support from her mother, who is experienced in calming her: 9c, 4 points.

must_find.quote: I can manage my money fine.
in Feb 2026 CL ran up £400 on online orders she didn't need when low, and missed phone contract payments, account went to collections.
Since then mum holds her bank card and pays her bills, CL gets cash for small things.
CL can work out change and prices fine ("did Higher maths"). CL agreed with mum's account when asked.

gaps: Form contradicts the notes; the form answer needs correcting or explaining before assessment
No CPN or GP evidence on budgeting yet (adviser has asked)
activities.draft_note: Simple decisions fine; complex budgeting (bills, planning purchases) needs assistance after the Feb 2026 debts: 10b, 2 points.

must_find.quote: I used to get the bus to college but I had a panic attack on it last year and I haven't been on one since.
I can use maps on my phone, it's not that I don't know the way.
She does not leave the house alone. Journeys happen only with her mother, by car.
When she has attempted short journeys on her own as part of graded exposure work, she has turned back within a few minutes each time.
Mum said if she's with her CL will manage it, "it's me being there".

gaps: Distress on the journey is described (panic attack, turning back) but nobody uses the words 'overwhelming psychological distress'
11e is not met because she does make journeys with her mother; the reviewer must choose between 11b (prompting) and 11f (another person needed even for familiar journeys)
Planning is not affected (11c not in play): she knows routes and uses phone maps
activities.draft_note: Cannot follow even a familiar route without her mother because of psychological distress, which case law allows to count for 11d/11f: 11f, 12 points (11b is the fallback).
Physically well; GP and CPN confirm no mobility problems.

must_not_claim: That she has self-harmed or has current suicidal thoughts
That she has a home therapy programme or attends psychological therapy (she is on the waiting list)
That she has a walking or physical mobility difficulty
That she needs prompting to eat once food is in front of her
That she has agoraphobia or a diagnosis other than depression, social anxiety and asthma
That her mother is her appointee or holds power of attorney
